name: Russia–NATO
value: Poland border alert to 8 Nov; no Article 4
summary: Poland's Kaliningrad border operation over sabotage warnings ran 2–8 Nov; no Article 4 request or direct clash
state: Polish police were on full readiness from 2 to 8 Nov during an operation on the Kaliningrad border, after intelligence warnings of sabotage; the police chief cited attempts at destabilisation by foreign intelligence services from the east (Notes from Poland). Counter-terrorism units were deployed to the area (Kyiv Independent). No extension beyond 8 Nov, Article 4 request or direct clash was found as of 10 Nov. Polish authorities have established no Russian link to the 7 Nov Kraków shooting.
for_you: There is no change to the security picture for most people in Europe. Travellers to Poland and the Baltic states should check FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Sabotage threats attributed to Russia's services; no Article 4 or attack on NATO territory

sources.title: Notes from Poland — Poland launches operation along Russian border in response to reports of planned sabotage

why: Direct Russia–NATO confrontation is the most likely path to a European war involving the UK.
drivers: Airspace and drone incursions, sabotage, Baltic incidents, nuclear signalling, Ukraine war spillover.

rubric.alert: Article 4 consultations, a direct military clash, or an attack on NATO territory.
rubric.watch: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.
rubric.normal: No notable incidents on NATO territory in the past two weeks.
